description: An operator installs a skill and later updates the binary — the installed skill is now at an older version with different methodology
naive_change: Add version field to skill front-matter and a check command that compares installed vs embedded
outcomes: skill versions remain consistent across binary updates

description: terminology.csv grows to 200+ terms and trait validation becomes prohibitively slow
naive_change: Add indexing or caching for the term set; keep term_set() as a HashSet for O(1) lookup
outcomes: the system validates each trait without blocking commits

description: Two operators run purpose-walk concurrently and both append to purposes.csv simultaneously
naive_change: CSV append is not atomic; add file locking or make append idempotent by checking for duplicate IDs
outcomes: concurrent stressor writes preserve data consistency

description: An operator runs residual init in a directory that already has partial residual/ data — some files exist some don't
naive_change: init must be idempotent: only write files that don't exist; never overwrite existing data
outcomes: init preserves existing attractor links when run in a populated directory

description: The token_warn limit is exceeded by a skill and no warning is surfaced
naive_change: Add token estimation check in skill-show and skill-list; warn when approaching token_warn from storage-config
outcomes: token warnings surface before any skill exceeds the warn limit

description: Terminology validation in the pre-commit hook becomes slow enough that operators bypass it with --no-verify, admitting unverified traits to the repository
naive_change: Build lexicon HashSet once per invocation; emit elapsed-time warning in verify output when the check exceeds 2 seconds
outcomes: trait validation completes without triggering hook avoidance

description: The skill install-and-check lifecycle creates ongoing maintenance burden — users must track, update, and reconcile installed stubs that could instead delegate all content to the binary
naive_change: Replace versioned installed stubs with static passthrough scripts that invoke the binary for content; remove version tracking from the installed file format
outcomes: skill stubs delegate content retrieval without requiring version management

description: An operator runs residual skill sessions on a preexisting project with no residual/ metadata — skills assume initialized data and produce empty or misleading outputs rather than pivoting to a capture-first mode
naive_change: Skills detect absence of stressors, purposes, and attractors at session start; skill-data warns and offers a bootstrapping checklist before proceeding to analysis
outcomes: skill sessions detect absent metadata before producing architecture analysis

description: A commit lands via --no-verify or direct CSV edit, bypassing the pre-commit hook — residuals data now contains unvalidated state that no skill session can safely trust as a baseline
naive_change: Skills inspect recent git log for commits that touched residual/ without a passing verify; surface the unverified window at session start and switch to a change-tracking focus before analysis
outcomes: skill sessions surface unverified stressor entries before analysis begins

description: Third-party libraries, generated files, and non-standard formats resist annotation — operators must manually edit CSVs, making tag-scan coverage readings misleading and creating false integrity signals
naive_change: Treat tag-scan as a suggestion system: allow stressor entries marked as coverage-exempt; tag-scan reports confidence rather than compliance; manual CSV edit is a first-class workflow, not a workaround
outcomes: stressor tagging acts as a suggestion rather than a hard coverage requirement

description: Stressor traits use plural and undefined terminology forms that fail verification, components exist only as free text with no registry, and no cross-store connectivity tests exist — data appears locally valid but fails as a system
naive_change: Add components.csv as a first-class registry; expand verify links to check component references; write unit tests asserting: stressor attractor_ids exist in attractors.csv, component names resolve in components.csv, and trait words resolve in terminology.csv
outcomes: attractor references remain valid across all residuals data stores

description: A trait references 'families' but terminology only defines 'family' — exact-word matching rejects valid plural, hyphenated, phrase, and language-variant forms like die/dice or alumnus/alumni, producing false violations that erode trust in verify
naive_change: Each lexicon entry carries a quoted alias list in addition to its canonical form; term_set expands all aliases; e.g. "'hyphenated-example' 'example-with-dash' 'this example has a dash in it' 'example, with hyphen'" all resolve to the same term for matching
outcomes: trait validation matches term aliases without penalizing plural or hyphenated variants

description: Projects want to store residuals data in TOML, JSON, SQLite, or a remote API — the CSV format is baked directly into every entity module with no I/O abstraction, making format migration require rewriting stressors, purposes, attractors, terminology, and personas separately
naive_change: Introduce storage-format + storage-migration behind storage; CSV is the initial implementation; format_version keys transfer; alternate backends deferred
outcomes: stressor data survives a storage format version migration keyed by a version number without loss or schema change

description: Stressors have no field for how to detect whether they have fired — neither the CSV schema nor the tag-scan system surfaces observable signals (log patterns, metric thresholds, git hook output) that indicate a stressor is active in the real system
naive_change: Add a detection_mechanism on stressor forces; field is free text describing observable signals that confirm the stressor is active (e.g. 'verify exits non-zero', 'git log shows --no-verify flag', 'matrix K/N > 1.0'); verify checks the field is non-empty for stressors targeting failing attractor pressure
outcomes: stressor entries declare detection mechanisms for observing attractor drift in practice

description: A stressor references a component name that has no entry in components.csv — the matrix displays a column for a component that has never been defined, described, or scoped, making the coupling analysis meaningless
naive_change: Require each residue component_id to resolve in components.csv before verify links passes; undefined component references are link violations; matrix columns come from residues against the registry
outcomes: stressor components resolve against a defined component registry before validation passes

description: An operator interprets residual components as code modules that must be fully implemented, or treats the component list as the actual system rather than a proposed architectural state space — adding five new components for comparison requires the same investment as the baseline, defeating the purpose of exploratory parallel architectures
naive_change: components.csv carries status (proposed / actual) and architecture_set; structure filter/group targets a set; matrix can render a single set or a diff across two sets
outcomes: operators explore proposed attractor states as named component sets without implying implementation

description: Stressor and purpose records embed component references directly in their fields — changing a component name or scope requires editing every stressor and purpose that mentions it; the 'which components survive this stressor' analysis has no dedicated home and cannot be versioned, compared, or queried independently
naive_change: residues.csv owns force_id × component_id; legacy components_affected/components_enabled stay transitional mirrors only; verify links checks residues against registry and force ids
outcomes: residue analysis is decoupled from stressor and purpose field definitions

description: An operator has accumulated many stressors, purposes, and components across concerns, teams, and parallel architecture sets — the flat matrix/list view with no grouping or subset filter makes relationships invisible and parallel architectures indistinguishable from the baseline; the operator cannot zoom to one attractor, architecture_set, or force cohort without reading the whole grid
naive_change: structure EXTERNAL filter/sort/group API (default group=attractor); matrix show accepts subset filters (--group, --architecture-set, force/component selectors) and renders a single set or all sets with visual section separators
outcomes: operators filter stressor and matrix views by group or architecture_set to inspect parallel architectures independently

description: residues.csv as designed in S-17 only carries stressor-sourced rows — purposes have no residue representation, making it impossible to see in one view which purposes are supported or undermined by which component and stressor combinations
naive_change: residues.csv force_id accepts both stressor and purpose ids via forces.csv; unified picture of how each component serves or fails across stress and intent
outcomes: residue records connect stressor and purpose entries within a unified group view

description: The CLI overwrites residues.csv (and other managed files) without checking for manual modifications — an operator who has annotated residue statuses, added notes, or rearranged rows loses those changes silently; no diff, no warning, no backup; the problem is sharpest for residues.csv but applies to all files
naive_change: storage-sessions change-detection hash; before write recompute and require --force on drift; storage-format performs the guarded CSV write
outcomes: residue files preserve manual modifications and surface diffs before any overwrite occurs

description: An operator trained on rigid phase-gated methodologies assumes skills must run in order, phases cannot overlap, and metadata must be complete before analysis — the tool does nothing to surface its fluent nature, causing operators to over-structure their workflow or abandon the tool as too prescriptive
naive_change: skill-data and CLI process text include fluent-usage notes; cli-help artifacts lead with the fluent entry model; skills describe themselves as analytical lenses rather than mandatory gates
outcomes: skill sessions communicate fluent stressor entry to counter phase-rigidity assumptions

description: Prospect skepticism of residuality efficacy blocks adoption — without robust studies and empirical alpha/beta perspective measures the method looks like ungrounded ceremony
naive_change: Design and execute controlled studies; derive and document alpha/beta; publish communicable robustness evidence alongside persona-walk defaults
outcomes: operator communicates residual-architecture robustness to a prospect via study and persona outcomes

description: Operator prematurely decides on a software fix for a stressor and never examines hardware, process, organization, or policy zig
naive_change: Skills and CLI remind the operator to examine whole-system-residue before software patches; reminder is incentive-aligned not foolproof
outcomes: operator examines whole-system-residue before recording a software-only naive change

description: Operator workflows are not considered — the tool demands a rigid full skill sequence and rejects a-la-carte use, so operators abandon residuality or fake compliance
naive_change: Make skill steps selectable; enforce residual structure via verify without mandating ceremony order
outcomes: operator uses residual a-la-carte without being forced through unused skill phases

description: Operator cannot tell why a stressor hurts the project because attractors lack paired positive and negative pressure — the stressor has nowhere coherent to land
naive_change: Require each attractor to define positive_state and negative_state; migrate off single-valence attractor classification
outcomes: operator links each stressor to an attractor that has both positive and negative state pressure

description: The NKP matrix is hard to read at dogfood scale — coupling heat does not read as a heatmap, row/column totals are missing or easy to lose, and headers/row labels scroll off-screen — so operators miss hyperliminal bands, fission candidates, and which forces drive K
naive_change: matrix show paints true background heat (not digit tint), always shows row/column/grand totals, supports --csv for external sticky viewers, and documents sticky header/label limits of the terminal table (or ships a pager/TUI path when the grid exceeds the viewport)
outcomes: operator reads coupling density, row/column totals, and force labels without losing orientation in the matrix viewport

description: residues.csv is already matrix-shaped (force × component cells), but at real project scale neither the CLI table nor raw CSV remains usable for filtering, zoom, multi-view exploration, or coherent landscape recall — spreadsheet-friendly shape alone does not yield operator fluency
naive_change: ship a human-centric landscape UX (local web or equivalent) with trivial filtering and multiple visualizations over the matrix-shaped residue store; keep CLI for capture and agentic work
outcomes: operator explores and filters residue coupling at project scale without re-reading the full CSV or CLI grid

description: Operators use conventional commit prefixes (fix:/chore:/refactor:) that carry no project vocabulary — git log drifts from lexicon and components.csv
naive_change: Add commit-msg hook with lexicon/component validation; block conventional commit types when commit_msg_enforce is true; allow general - override
outcomes: operator commits omit defined outcome from subjects

description: Agent or operator edits residual/ CSVs directly (Python scripts, raw text edits, sed) for operations the residual CLI already supports — bypassing ID generation, idempotency guards, and verify
naive_change: CLAUDE.md instructs agents to use residual CLI for all data operations; verify detects drift from direct mutation; force_id generation and idempotency remain owned by the tool
outcomes: operator uses residual add for all force additions; direct CSV mutation is only used for operations the CLI does not support

description: When persona voices are generated inline alongside the main conversation they read the same context, share the same mental model, and produce shallow concerns that mirror what the operator already thinks — producing no new information and failing to surface real stressor pressure from external viewpoints
naive_change: Persona walks in later phases use isolated subagents to prevent context pollution; each persona subagent runs staged analysis without reading the main session context
outcomes: personas are given their own space to develop genuine concerns; context pollution and groupthink-esque effects from shared session context are prevented

description: An agent prompted to bootstrap an uninitialized ledger conflates an attractor with the system mission statement — bundling multiple concerns and omitting the negative state — producing a ledger that appears populated but carries no bifurcation signal for stressors to push against
naive_change: Bootstrap guidance in skill-data explicitly defines what an attractor is and is not, flags the mission-statement anti-pattern, and requires both positive and negative state before proceeding
outcomes: operator records attractor with distinct positive and negative state before recording stressors

description: A stressor fires but the components listed on it did not need to change — the force-component mapping was anticipated incorrectly. Over time these mismatches accumulate unchecked: the matrix coupling analysis drifts from empirical reality, and no record exists to identify or correct the pattern
naive_change: Skills prompt recording of which components actually changed when a stressor fires; skill-data surfaces an attractor occurrence log so force-component mappings can be empirically refined over time
outcomes: operator records actual component changes per stressor occurrence; attractor occurrence logs accumulate for empirical refinement

description: At time of use, the agent encounters existing records and examples that use naive_change for assumptions, untreated behavior, and mechanistic adjustments interchangeably.
naive_change: Present field-specific examples that separate environmental force, mechanistic adjustment, desired outcome, and unchecked attractor state.
outcomes: Agent records a concrete system adjustment under naive_change. Agent leaves desired end states under outcome.

description: At time of use, an actor supplies an incident or requirement narrative framed entirely through known components, concealing whether any force originates beyond the architecture iteration ergodic boundary.
naive_change: Add an optional post-capture ergodic review that uses component terminology to ask whether the force primarily exists beyond the boundary.
outcomes: Agent identifies the narrative as a component dynamic or asks the actor to identify the force beyond the ergodic boundary before recording a stressor.

description: At time of use, an actor identifies a whole-system adjustment that answers a stressor, but authority, ownership, budget, culture, or timing places that adjustment outside current control.
naive_change: Preserve the preferred whole-system-residue, ask what lies within actor control or influence, and record an actionable interim residue without presenting it as equivalent. Organization/process zig: preserve preferred architecture while distinguishing immediately actionable change.
outcomes: Actor retains the whole-system-residue as a future architectural direction. Actor records an actionable residue that moves the system toward the desired outcome within current influence.

description: At time of use, an actor brings a risk-analysis convention in which outcome means the adverse consequence of a stressor into residual force capture.
naive_change: Prompt separately for the system adjustment, desired outcome, and attractor state reached when pressure goes unchecked.
outcomes: Actor records the desired state preserved under the stressor. Actor uses the attractor negative state to describe unchecked pressure.

description: A varied audience produces distinct operating contexts and event sequences, but actor-controlled analytics combine them into aggregate measurements that conceal state transitions.
naive_change: Add contextual and sequential drill-down views to the analytics system.
outcomes: Actor discovers stressors and attractors concealed by aggregate measurements.

description: A varied audience produces distinct operating contexts and event sequences, but externally controlled analytics expose only aggregate measurements and the actor cannot alter their collection or presentation.
naive_change: During a requested landscape review, the skill asks which contexts, sequences, and transitions the aggregates may conceal.
outcomes: Actor extracts additional force configurations from the available aggregate evidence.

description: Actor-controlled analytics rank observations by frequency and suppress less common coherent event sequences.
naive_change: Add a view that preserves distinct event sequences without applying a frequency admission threshold.
outcomes: Actor evaluates coherent stressors without requiring observed frequency or probability-framing.

description: Organizational or third-party analytics expose frequency-ranked observations while preventing the actor from changing collection, ranking, or retention.
naive_change: During a requested analytics review, the skill asks which coherent sequences may be absent from the frequency-ranked evidence.
outcomes: Actor considers coherent stressors despite limitations in the analytics control plane.

description: As the ledger grows, precise agent session memory favors IDs while operator longitudinal memory retains names and concepts, causing ID-only references to break conversational continuity.
naive_change: Instruct skills to use attractor names and force shortnames conversationally while retaining IDs in executable commands.
outcomes: Operator follows force and attractor references without external lookup. Agent preserves exact command targeting.

description: Laws, handbooks, contracts, or established practices change after research is captured, while an actor later consults the superseded material during a walk.
naive_change: When research is requested, the skill asks whether selected material remains applicable and surfaces conflicting dates or claims for operator judgment.
outcomes: Actor revises stressors and attractors when current environmental evidence contradicts recorded research.

description: Authoritative research describes nominal behavior while exceptions and undocumented practices shape the environment, causing documented order to appear exhaustive.
naive_change: During requested research review, the skill asks what observed or coherent behavior exists outside the selected sources and challenges their use as an admission boundary.
outcomes: Actor admits coherent stressors that are absent from or contradicted by documented order.

description: An actor requests a broad research review whose volume, conflicts, or irrelevant detail displaces the active force and attractor context from the agent working context.
naive_change: Before reviewing research, the agent asks which question and material should be examined, then reviews bounded selections without automatically carrying the full corpus forward.
outcomes: Agent and operator retain shared comprehension of the active walk while selected research informs it.

description: Repeated patterns in research appear stable enough that an actor treats them as a complete predictive model of the hyperliminal and dismisses contradictory configurations as noise.
naive_change: During research review, the skill asks what the apparent model fails to explain and preserves coherent contradictions as candidate forces or attractors.
outcomes: Actor uses patterned evidence without excluding stressors or attractors that contradict the inferred model.

description: Project work proceeds without a regular cadence of architecture walks. As real-world force configurations evolve between reviews, recorded stressors and attractors remain static and the residual-architecture loses correspondence with its environment.
naive_change: A non-blocking pre-commit hook compares last purpose-walk and stressor-walk completion against an operator-defined interval; state in .walk-review.toml on the git-sidecar branch; guru walk-reminder snippets supply copy; operator records completed or deferred via residual walk record.
outcomes: Actor routinely revises and extends stressors and attractors as new evidence builds.

description: An operator invokes a skill with whatever model is available to them — frontier, mid-tier, local, or open-weight — and that model's capability falls short of the skill's cognitive demands. The failure is visible, not silent, but locating the floor and working around it costs the operator manual effort on every occurrence.
naive_change: Stress-test each skill against a matrix of degraded/open-weight models pre-release (James-Phoenix floor-finding); encode the discovered floor as skill metadata; lower the floor itself by preferring worked examples over reasoning prose in skill authoring.
outcomes: operator locates skill floor without manual triage

description: Frontier-tier model access becomes economically inviable — pricing, provider exits, or a broader AI-investment contraction — leaving operators with only slower, less capable, open-weight models. When frontier capability disappears, the procedural burden an LLM agent used to absorb lands on the human operator instead.
naive_change: Build an agent-optional UX surface (TUI first, web UI as stretch) and author skill variants runnable by lesser agents, so procedural burden doesn't fall entirely on the human when frontier access disappears.
outcomes: operator completes residual processes without substantial strain or LLM assistance

description: Some system architecture environments — air-gapped networks, classified or regulated systems, data-residency-restricted deployments — prohibit outbound access to hosted frontier models entirely for security-policy reasons. Operators inside these environments must accomplish the same cognitive work using only local or approved models, with no path to frontier-tier capability regardless of budget.
naive_change: Build an agent-optional UX surface (TUI first, web UI as stretch) and author skill variants runnable by lesser agents.
outcomes: operator completes a skill session using only locally-approved models

description: An operator is already convinced of residuality's value, but their org's prevailing methodology culture treats upfront stressor/attractor analysis as heretical or waterfall-flavored. Surfacing residuality vocabulary directly risks the operator's standing, so they conceal, dilute, or avoid the method even though they're sold on it.
naive_change: Translation layer — express naive_change/outcome in the org's native methodology vocabulary (TDD, DDD, Clean/Onion, etc.) rather than exposing residuality jargon directly.
outcomes: operator presents architecture reasoning without exposing residuality vocabulary

description: Engineers whose ethos rejects in-codebase documentation treat @residue:/@stressor: tags as unwelcome clutter — not from skepticism about residuality's value, but from the same standing/cultural-hostility pressure that makes surfacing residuality vocabulary risky elsewhere in the org. Manual annotation never happens in that environment, so tag-based residue tracking is dead on arrival.
naive_change: git-sidecar: Store the full residual/ metadata tree on an orphan git branch (Entire.io-style); config may live in ../residual/config.toml (stealth-mode) one directory above the repo so working-branch commits never touch residual config; verify resolves ledger from sidecar tip; storage-migration lifts inline residual/ to sidecar; working_tree_policy warns when residual/ is staged on the working branch.
outcomes: operator maintains a residue ledger without editing the working branch

description: An outsider with motive — a political rival, an executive looking to kill the initiative, an auditor — discovers raw residuality artifacts (walks, attractor language, candid failure narratives) and reads them not neutrally but as ammunition. The danger isn't that the reasoning is unfinished; it's that the observer's locked priors turn even sound reasoning into a weapon against the operator.
naive_change: Theorize which artifacts are safe for which audiences before any raw ledger content becomes externally visible, routing only vetted translated artifacts into channels a hostile outsider could reach.
outcomes: operator restricts raw walk artifacts from hostile outsider visibility

description: A walk can satisfy nominal headcount (e.g. P-10's stakeholder + direct-user bar) while a hierarchical or blame-driven team culture suppresses genuine dissent — junior voices defer to senior ones, minority concerns carry social cost, candid failure-mode naming gets punished rather than rewarded. Conversely, a psychologically safe team can still lack headcount or role diversity — everyone present shares the same exposure to the system and simply hasn't seen what a different role would surface. Either gap alone produces a walk that feels thorough — attendance met, atmosphere felt open — but isn't: neither condition alone guarantees recorded stressors reflect the real state space.
naive_change: Document that headcount and psychological safety are independently necessary and neither is sufficient alone, so operators at least know what genuine coverage requires.
outcomes: operator's walk achieves both headcount and psychological safety, not one alone

description: AI vendors increasingly train on overlapping public corpora and converge through similar RLHF alignment processes. An operator who assigns different personas to different models, expecting genuine perspective divergence, gets convergent reasoning and risk-posture back anyway — the diversity they believe 'multiple models' bought them is illusory, because the vendors themselves are subject to the same competitive and training pressures that narrowed the field to begin with.
naive_change: Track which model/vendor family backed each persona in personas.csv; verify flags a walk where all personas trace to the same vendor family, surfacing the illusory-diversity case mechanically instead of relying on the operator to notice.
outcomes: operator's walk draws personas from more than one model vendor family

description: Group discussion collapses independent perspectives toward whatever position surfaces first or carries the most social weight, before any of it reaches the ledger — the record ends up looking like consensus even when consensus was never actually tested.
naive_change: Capture each participant's input in isolation before synthesis, reconciling independent submissions into the shared ledger only afterward; a later TUI/GUI networking layer can support this at scale for human teams.
outcomes: operator captures each participant's input independently before synthesis

description: A purpose that reads as safely supporting the positive attractor may, under sustained adversarial pressure, turn out to produce the opposite effect. Most challenges will be trivially overturned, but the walk needs the capacity to catch the ones that aren't.
naive_change: Assign a devil's-advocate role to at least one persona/participant per walk, explicitly arguing toward the negative attractor regardless of personal belief; record whether each purpose is confirmed or found to invert.
outcomes: operator's walk records whether each purpose is confirmed or inverted under adversarial argument

description: As the ledger grows past what an operator can hold in working memory, coherent longitudinal grasp of the landscape degrades — the operator records duplicate or contradictory forces, or makes decisions blind to what's already there, because re-reading 40+ stressors before every session isn't viable.
naive_change: A quizzing/spaced-repetition mode (residual quiz?) that periodically Socratically tests operator recall of attractors/stressors/purposes, keeping their mental model synced with the store's growth.
outcomes: operator recalls the current force landscape without re-reading the store

description: Residuality has little presence in model pretraining corpora, so an agent's prior on residual's CLI conventions (cwd-relative storage, config-driven paths) is weak. When other configured instructions for the same agent — e.g. a Cursor rule directing use of nix develop, or a different project's skill/tooling conventions — pull the agent toward a different working context, the agent applies residual commands from the wrong directory without noticing the mismatch, and the target project's ledger data lands in an unrelated repository instead.
naive_change: Surface the resolved config path (including parent-dir stealth-mode and git-sidecar branch), storage root, and owning project prominently in every residual command's output, so an operator or agent notices immediately when data is about to land somewhere unexpected.
outcomes: operator's residual commands resolve to the correct project's storage path

description: A single, fixed-name git-sidecar branch stores metadata for every working branch in the repo, so switching feature branches doesn't switch which metadata tip is being read or written.
naive_change: Keep one fixed git_sidecar_branch name in config for the entire repo and trust operators to remember which feature branch each residue narrative belongs to.
outcomes: residues describe the wrong working branch | operator loses track of which branch a stressor belongs to
